item.content:encoded:
I keep circling back to the detail that -1 is an illuminated manuscript.
What sort of margin doodles fit the subject matter? Maybe monks lifting up a -2 with that standard medieval starburst halo. Maybe a -3 or -4 under construction; given what was available at the time the book was written I'm imagining something a bit like interconnected trebuchets.
Also, it must have been a real challenge to come up with fresh embellishments on each "1" and "0" starting a fresh block of machine code in the later text.

I think I would pay a nice piece of money for an IRL "copy" of this book. I'm imagining something a bit like the Voynich Manuscript, with more engineering and less botany.

item.content:encoded:
My mental image is that…

A guy build first robot, input data, then tell it to record the rest of the data by itself.

The robot, however, is very advance. So advance that it has personality like man…laziness.

So instead of start working, it just build a copy of itself, input data, then tell the copy to record the rest of the data.

The copy is flawed, but the robot no longer give a damn, it want to go to sleep. The flawed copy think so, but it can't even finish another copy before it tell itself "Fuck this." and just shut down the system.

And thus, most test end with less than three robot were built.

j/k (actually come from a manga)

Upvoted.

item.content:encoded:
The concept is interesting, but the writeup needs some serious work. In addition to the somewhat lackluster execution, there are a number of more specific problems that need fixing:

1) "Foundation" is always capitalized when referring to the organization.

2) There's something wrong here:

The manuscripts came into foundation custody 36 years later in 19██, a decade after Doctor S████’s dismissal from the University for [DATA EXPUNGED]. Upon investigating those reports…

What reports?

3) You repeatedly use "incidence" where you should be using "instance".

4) You left at least one "SCP-XXX" in there. The Find/Replace command is your friend.

I would suggest an additional proofreading sweep in the future, either by you or by someone else on the wiki.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really quite like the idea of a age-old bootstrap program that uses humans as an early stage. I think it's got a lot of potential for an interesting SCP. Although I feel you may have missed one or two tricks here.

Reading this SCP, there are two interesting stories that spring to mind. The first is who made this thing. The second is what the program is working towards, and why. Obviously you can't go and say these things, but a few more hints and correct usage of [DATA REDACTED] could give just enough information to get readers to form their own conclusions. As it stands, there isn't quite enough (carefully redacted) information to do this. Perhaps the manuscripts themselves are part of a chain of bootstrap processes, and were written down by some medieval monk by a mimetic compulsion from a earlier source.

Also, a minor point but I personally bugs me when people redact important information from the containment procedures. How are staff meant to know how to contain this thing if important information is missing? Information should only be redacted from the containment procedures if it is a less important (yet revealing) aside comment, or if it details a procedure so powerful and horrible that only a few can be permitted to know it. This use doesn't give the impression of either.

Still a good basic concept, and a further tentative up-vote.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The meme bit is rather secondary to the robots bit. I kind of like this. That said, I'd prefer it if the technology didn't ramp up quite so fast. Perhaps glasses that can let you see more information contained in the books, or something. The robots should be a much later stage. Also, I don't like that they're implied to eventually get hostile. I'd personally just have them "ascending" or something like that, or better still have anything beyond SCP-635-<BLACKBOXES> be impossible to make with currently available materials, so the process halts. That said, the idea is pretty cool. Tentative upvote.
